To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the esterification and hydrolysis of the steroid hormones is not related to the biological activity of the hormones.
the C-21-fatty acid ester of cortisone, cortisone-21-stearoyl ester, is a very weak ligand of the glucocorticosteroid receptor, and that it is hydrolyzed very rapidly by liver esterase.

the biological activities of the C-21-fatty acid ester metabolite of corticosterone are not significantly different from that of the unesterified hormone and that the ester is hydrolyzed very rapidly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological activity of fatty acid esters of steroids.
the metabolism, transport and biological action of fatty acid esters of steroid hormones.
the biological activity of steroid hormones and their metabolites, particularly those that have an ester linkage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the esterification and hydrolysis of the corticosteroids are a dynamic equilibrium, which is in contrast to the situation with the esters of the estrogen, where the esterification is a slow process and the hydrolysis a rapid one.
the C-21 esters of the corticosteroids are inactive in vivo.
the esterification does not appear to be a means of increasing the biological activity or the duration of response of the corticosteroids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fatty acid esters of corticoids are not potent inducers of gluconeogenesis.
the C-21-fatty acid ester of cortisone is an extremely potent glucocorticoid in vivo, but is not a ligand for the glucocorticoids receptor in vitro.
the esters are not active in vivo, but are rapidly hydrolyzed to their parent compounds, which are then responsible for the observed biological activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biological activity of steroid esters is not necessarily a simple reflection of the properties of the parent hormone.
the esters of steroids are not likely to be the biologically active forms of the hormones, but rather are intermediates in the catabolism of the steroid hormones.
the C-21 fatty acid esters of corticoids are poor ligands for the glucocorticoids receptor.
